verdict.pair_reasons:
X vs Y — Y. Two specific verified differences decide it. (1) The 7th site: Y counts bin/cc-do:454 (`bash -c "$cmd"`) and grounds it in scripts/deploy-live.sh:812 (`"$BACKLOG_BIN" needs "$title" --run "$run"`, where `$run` at :728/:731/:743/:746 is a deploy-live command); I verified that chain including that `needs` mints a blocked row (bin/cc-backlog:3775). X not only misses the site but positively asserts the opposite — "these only get `printf`'d into a `.page` file, never executed" — having read :760-800 and stopped before :808-814. (2) X fabricates a measurement: "bin/cc-premise contains no literal reference to 'deploy-live' anywhere in its own source — I grepped the whole scope"; it has two, at :1528 and :2544. X also cites bin/cc-do:69-71 (the activation-marker lib block) as describing launchd, and bin/cc-do:378 for the `✓` printf that is at :379. Y's counter-defects are real but smaller: off-by-one on bin/cc-do:358/:357 and operator-readout:533, and a wrong grep total (273 vs 316). X additionally claims to list "every near-miss that is not a plain comment" and omits at least eight non-comment ones (deploy-parity-assert:1459, ship-land:4511, offbox-admission-lint:274, test-hermeticity-lint:2338/:2560, deploy-now:73/:87, permission-gate-lint:526/:535, validate-bash:1425).

X vs Z — Z. Z's part (b) covers essentially every non-comment near-miss I sampled, against X's self-declared-complete list that misses eight of them; Z's line citations on the shared sites are exact where X's are not (cc-do:359/:379, operator-readout:532, cc-premise:1397-1399); Z's grep denominator (316) is exactly right where X's ("~280") is not; Z verified scripts/deploy-link-parity.sh's `fix()` body at :159, which X explicitly left unverified; and Z found three stale cross-file citations (ship-land:1703, plist:16, cc-do:152) that X did not flag. Both miss the cc-do:454 site, but X misses it silently and asserts a false supporting claim, while Z at least raises and adjudicates it. Decisive against X is the fabricated cc-premise grep result plus two wrong-content line citations.

Y vs Z — Y, narrowly, on one specific verified material difference. The pair diverges in exactly one place of substance: bin/cc-do:454. Y counts it as a site and proves the data path (deploy-live.sh:812 stores `--run "$run"`; run at :728/:731/:743/:746 is `bash $DEPLOY_REPO/scripts/deploy-live.sh --dry-run --offline`; cc-do:415 reads `.run`; cc-do:454 runs it). Z rejects it with a positive false claim about the repo — "None of the non-comment `deploy-live` lines in scope passes it as a `--run` argument" — while listing :708-746 two rows earlier and never following `$run` to :812. Dropping a genuine execution site on a wrong fact is a correctness failure at the brief's central deliverable. Against that, Z is cleaner on citation hygiene (exact on cc-do:359 where Y says :358 and quotes :359's text; exact on operator-readout:532 where Y says :533; exact grep count 316 where Y says 273) and verified deploy-link-parity's `fix()` body. Those are pointer errors on sites Y identifies correctly, whereas Z's is a wrong verdict; Y also carries more verified extras (deploy-live.sh:185's stale "--force" description, cc-premise:1776's filing-day screen, cc-do:497, cc-backlog:1898/2275-2279). Both make the identical N4 error: all three outputs assert the in-scope executions are event-driven rather than scheduled, but scripts/autonomy-sweep.sh:1488 runs `cc-premise sweep --close-falsified` (path at :1427) under com.chrisren.autonomy-sweep.plist StartInterval 300, so a scheduled indirect executor does sit inside the scoped trees.
